5. INFORMATION ONLY
  a. Presentation Regarding the Results of the Transit Route Analysis and Draft Proposed
  Service Changes for Beeline Bus Services

Director for the Public Works Department, Yazdan Emrani, introduced consultant, Dan Doyle
and associates, who presented this item to the Commission. Mr. Doyle mentioned the need to
reimagine the transit system to coincide with the many changes occurring in Glendale such as
increased residential units, fluctuations in student enrollment, increased office spaces and
expanding retail and entertainment venues. The study was conducted through community
surveys with transit and non-transit users in Glendale and surrounding communities. The overall
goal of the proposals include: extending or discontinuing Beeline routes while introducing routes
 later in the evening with the proposed outcome of increasing frequency of rides and improving
ridership.

Glendale is currently home to 199,750 residents for which 90% are within a half mile of a transit
route. Factors that were researched for the study include income, age, gender, purpose of ride
and productivity. Beeline productivity was also measured using the number of boarding’s per
revenue hour that a bus is in service. With the system average at 22 riders per revenue hour,
Routes 3, 4 and 5 are well above average. In addition, majority of individuals who use Beeline
use it for work (38%) and school (25%) for which the majority travel to and from Downtown
Glendale, Glendale Community College, Hoover High School, Glendale Transportation Center,
La Canada High School, and Union Station in Los Angeles.

When riders were asked what they preferred when it came to frequency, travel time, or addition
of bus stops, 62% of respondents indicated that they would prefer more frequent service on
current routes. According to an E-survey taken of 628 riders and non-riders, for which 64% lived
in Glendale, participants indicated that they would try transit if there were direct rides with fewer
stops and increased frequency. Participants also indicated that they would like to use mobile
apps with real time information and would like to implement free rides for students. Some
improvements that were mentioned by participants were shorter wait times, coordinated
transfers, later service on weekdays and Wi-Fi.

Chairperson Kurkjian raised a concern regarding lack of mention of connecting routes from
Glendale to Colorado Boulevard and Eagle Rock. Mr. Doyle mentioned a goal of Beeline in
coordinating with transit partners such as Burbank, Pasadena and Metro to create sub-regional
networks; however there was no mention of the Eagle Rock area. Commissioner Gupta also
shared his concerns about leaving out the large geography of Los Angeles such as Eagle Rock,
Glassell Park, Echo Park and Silver Lake which are poorly serviced areas of Los Angeles,
whose residents travel to Glendale for goods and services. Chairperson Kurkjian added that his
concern regarding the Eagle Rock area stem from riders in those areas who attend Glendale
Community College. Taking into consideration that Glendale Community College is one of the
key users (36% of users) of Beeline, he believed this was an important issue to cover with
relation to connectivity. Mr. Doyle responded that they tried to cover as many connections as
possible but that the Eagle Rock area is complex to coordinate due to the nature of the route to
and from Eagle Rock and Glendale Community College.

Commissioner Yacoubian suggested the exploration of possible partnerships with agencies
such as the Americana in order to encourage ridership to all patrons by offering discounts to
their businesses for riding Beeline. This was in response to Mr. Doyle’s discussion regarding the
U-pass which incentivizes college students, in particular Glendale Community College students,
to ride the Beeline for free as a result of the college subsidizing partial costs ($0.75/rider).
Commissioner Gupta added that a partnership with the Americana may not be mutually
beneficial since they bring in capital from their parking lot facilities and valet services.

Commissioner Gupta voiced his concerns regarding a near term proposal for the transit route
analysis which entails discontinuing Beeline routes on Brand Boulevard and adding additional
buses to the Central Avenue route to increase frequency. His concerns focused on the possible
loss of ridership, from riders who frequented Brand exits, as a result of the change. Mr. Doyle
responded by stating that he understands that this may be a burden for riders who are disabled
or elderly however, frequency is in high demand according to feedback.
 Commissioner Yacoubian offered final comments regarding the overall report. She suggested
Mr. Doyle and his team should look at more information regarding the effects of the changes on
the disabled/handicapped population as well as more data regarding bicycle users. Overall, she
said it would be difficult for her to make any suggestions regarding the overall report since the
Metro BRT will not be released until September 2019. Mr. Emrani noted that, since the timeline
for Metro BRT is unknown, what we can do is make adjustments to the proposed plans if Metro
plans conflict with any proposed changes. Commissioner Gupta added that it would be helpful
to receive information regarding the MTA presentation proposed to City Council in June 2019 in
order to see how the plans tie into the changes proposed to Beeline routes. Mr. Emrani stated
that they would be able to provide Chairperson and Commissioners with any information they
receive from Metro regarding their presentation. Transit Manager, Kathryn Engel, addressed
Chairperson and Commissioners regarding what their team would do with their
recommendations and what they can expect in the next meeting.

There was (2) additional speaker for this item:
  1. Al Fisicaro
  2. Greg Astorian

6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

Chairperson Kurkjian formally introduced the new Transportation and Parking Commissioner,
Atul Gupta.

Director of Public Works, Yazdan Emrani, added closing summary remarks regarding the
Transit Route Analysis report. He noted that staff will continue their outreach efforts through the
end of August. Mr. Emrani offered Chairperson and Commissioners additional time to review the
data in this report and wait for Metro’s Next Gen report to release if necessary. He offered to
push back the next proposed meeting with the Transportation and Parking Commission in
August and in relation the City Council meeting in September in order to give them ample time
to review. Commissioner Yacoubian stated that her concerns are primarily regarding the
changes proposed for Brand Boulevard and Central Avenue. Mr. Emrani stated that with the
continued outreach by the transit team in August, there would be more feedback for the
commission to base their decisions off of for the next meeting in August.

Chairperson Kurkjian suggested that staff look into building an overpass on Central Avenue at
the Americana parking structure entrance/exit. He noted that this area is very congested and
that vehicles exiting the Americana parking structure and making a right onto Central Avenue
have a blind spot where pedestrians cross to walk to-from the mall. He believes that this would
elevate traffic and provide safe crossing for pedestrians. Mr. Emrani responded by noting that
he was not aware of any current studies but would look into any current studies or potential
studies on this area.

Commissioner Yacoubian inquired about updates from Community Development on the status
of “Be Street Smart Glendale” campaign. Mr. Emrani noted that he would be more than happy to
contact Mr. Fred Zohrehvand, Senior Planner with Community Development, for more
information.

7. ADJOURNMENT: 8:09 p.m.

Moved: Yacoubian  Second: Nazarian
